q: 51. Evaluation of building is done based on
explain: Preliminary evaluation of a building's cost is typically calculated using the plinth area rate of similar structures in the locality.

q: 52. Centre line method is specially adopted for estimating.......... buildings.
explain: The center line method is versatile and efficient for various geometric shapes, including circular and polygonal buildings.

q: 53. *Centre-line method is used for calculation of
explain: This method is used to calculate quantities for any structure where the walls or perimeters follow a consistent center line.

q: 54. In long and short wall method of estimation, the length of long wall is the center to center space between walls plus
options: half of the breadth of wall on each side
one forth of the breadth of wall on each side
explain: The formula for the length of a long wall is (C/C length + 2 x half width), which equals C/C length + one full breadth.

q: 55. Payment of the steel is done by
explain: While small quantities use quintals, large scale steel procurement and payment are standardly measured in Metric Tonnes (MT).

q: 56. Normally which one contract gives the maximum value of project
explain: An item rate contract often leads to a higher project value as every individual unit of work is measured and paid for based on actual execution.

q: 57. *The volume of C.A required to make 100 m^3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: Due to voids and shrinkage, roughly 150-154 m^3 of dry material is needed for 100 m^3 wet concrete. For a 1:2:4 mix, coarse aggregate is 4/7 of that dry volume.

q: 58. Compute the amount of cement required for 10 m^3 RCC having M20 (1:1.5:3).
explain: All options are mathematically equivalent for this mix ratio once converted between volume, bags, and weight.

q: 59. The amount of cement required in 10 m^3 concrete having 1:2:3 ratio
explain: Based on the standard 1.54 shrinkage factor, a 1:2:3 mix (total 6 parts) for 10 m^3 requires approximately 70-72 bags.

q: 60. The amount of cement required per cubic meter having mix (1:3:6)
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix, cement is 1/10 of the dry volume. For 1 m^3 wet, we use ~1.54 m^3 dry, resulting in approx 4.3 bags.

q: 61. *Of the total estimated cost a building, the cost of electrification usually accounts
explain: Electrical installations are generally estimated as 8% of the total building cost.

q: 62. The c/s area (mm^2) and unit weight (kg/m) of 16 mm steel bar is respectively
explain: Area = πr² = 201 mm². Unit weight = D²/162 = 16²/162 ≈ 1.58 kg/m.

q: 63. *Compound amount of Rs. 100 in 4 years @ 4% interest
explain: Using A = P(1 + r/100)^n, 100(1.04)^4 is approximately 116.98, rounded to 117.

q: 64. The quantity of cement required for 1 m^3 plaster C:S(1:5) ratio
explain: Calculating dry mortar volume and cement portion results in approximately 310 kg.

q: 65. The amount of cement required for 1 m^3 mortar (1:6) plaster
explain: Using standard shrinkage and wastage factors for 1:6 mortar, the cement required is roughly 265 kg.

q: 66. The actual weight of cement bag is more in case of
explain: Paper bags prevent the 'seepage' or loss of fine cement particles better than woven bags, maintaining weight better.

q: 67. In the detailed estimate the areas are worked out to the nearest
explain: Standard practice in quantity surveying is to record areas to two decimal places (0.01 m^2).

q: 68. In the detailed estimate the volumes are worked out to the nearest
explain: Volumes are calculated with higher precision, usually to three decimal places (0.01 m^3).

q: 69. In the center-line method of working out volumes, for cross walls what deductions must be made from the center line length at each junction?
explain: At a T-junction, half the breadth of the wall is deducted from the total center line length to avoid double counting.

q: 70. *The unit rate of items written by the contractor in BOQ is in numeral as well as alphabetical form. Which one is preferred?
explain: Words (alphabetical) are preferred to prevent tampering or ambiguity with numbers in legal tender documents.

q: 71. Which is considered in the calculation of plinth area?
explain: Plinth area includes the wall thickness and internal circulation spaces like corridors.

q: 72. Which is not considered in the calculation of plinth area?
explain: Uncovered projections or cantilevered beams outside the wall line are excluded from the plinth area.

q: 73. There is a room size of 4m x 5m x 3m height having opening for ventilation is 0.75m x 0.75m, then total plaster for ceiling is
explain: Ceiling plaster area is simply Length x Breadth (4 x 5 = 20 m^2). Openings in walls do not affect ceiling area.

q: 74. The plan of a building is in the from of a rectangle with centerline dimension of outer walls as 9.7m x 14.7m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30m. Then its plinth area is
75. *In the case of unsewered areas, an additional provision for septic tank is usually
explain: Standard estimates add 3-4% for sanitary and water supply works including septic tanks.

q: 76. The capacity of a flushing cistern is normally
explain: Standard domestic low-level flushing cisterns have a capacity of 12-15 liters.

q: 77. The volume of cement required to prepare 100 cubic metre of 1 : 2 : 4 concrete is
explain: Dry volume = 154 m^3. Cement = 154 / (1+2+4) = 154 / 7 = 22 m^3 (Option d is the closest answer provided in the key).

q: 78. During the calculation of RCC the amount of steel deducted is
explain: In standard concrete volume calculations, the volume of steel reinforcement is not deducted.

q: 79. Arrange the specific weights of wood (w), cement (c), steel (s) and coarse aggregate (A) in increasing order
explain: Typical densities: Wood (~600-800), Cement (1440), Aggregate (~1600), Steel (7850 kg/m^3).

q: 80. *1 British gallon = ........litres.
explain: The Imperial (British) gallon is defined as 4.54609 liters.

q: 81. One US Gallon =
explain: The US liquid gallon is smaller than the British gallon, equaling 3.785 liters.

q: 82. One dharmi is equivalent to
explain: A 'dharmi' is a local unit of measurement, standardly taken as 2.40 kg in this context.

q: 83. Which one is incorrect with respect to measurement of area of land?
explain: All the listed conversions for Bigha, Katha, and Ropani are standard accepted values in Nepal.

q: 84. *One Ropani =
explain: One Ropani is equal to 5476 square feet, which is approximately 1.502 Katha.

q: 85. 1 He = .....Ropani.
explain: One hectare is approximately equal to 19.6 Ropani.

q: 86. *An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: A hectare is a square with 100-meter sides, totaling 10,000 m^2.

q: 87. One hectare –meter represents a volume of
explain: 1 Hectare (10,000 m^2) x 1 meter depth = 10,000 m^3.

q: 88. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per meter length is equal to
explain: Weight = D²/162 = 100/162 ≈ 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62.

q: 89. The weight of 12mm diameter mild steel per meter length is equal to
90. How many kilo-liters are in one cubic meter?
explain: 1 m^3 = 1000 liters. Since 1000 liters = 1 kilo-liter, 1 m^3 = 1 kL.

q: 91. Which method is easiest for the estimation of the quantity of material?
explain: The center line method is generally faster and easier as it involves a single continuous length.

q: 92. What is the minimum period for which the lime concrete in foundation be left wet without the construction of masonry over it?
explain: Lime concrete requires a curing period of at least 7 days before building upon it.

q: 93. *The plan of a building is in the form of rectangle with center line dimension of outer walls as 9.7m x 14.7m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30m. Then its carpet area is
explain: Carpet area = Inner dimensions. (9.7-0.3) x (14.7-0.3) = 9.4 x 14.4 = 135.36 m^2.

q: 94. The volume of cement required for 10 m^3 of brick work in 1:6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: 10 m^3 brickwork requires ~3 m^3 mortar. Cement = 3 / (1+6) = 3/7 m^3.

q: 95. *Contractor profit is added to
explain: Contractor's profit is included during the rate analysis phase for individual items.

q: 96. *The rate analysis induces
options: material, labour, contractor's overhead and profit
explain: Comprehensive rate analysis must account for materials, labor, overheads, and the contractor's profit margin.

q: 97. The overheads and profit claimed by the contractor to client is
explain: These costs are not billed separately but are embedded into the unit rates of the work items.

q: 98. For the approval of any project a no. of sanction is followed out. Which one is initially done?
explain: Administrative sanction is the formal acceptance of the project proposal by the department before technical details are finalized.

q: 99. *The main target of a contractor is to
explain: While a contractor must complete the work, the primary business objective is to maximize profit.

q: 100. *The chairman of material rate fixation committee in district is
explain: In the Nepalese administrative system, the Chief District Officer (CDO) chairs the committee that fixes district material rates.
